concepts.label: CAS (Compare-And-Swap) Optimistic Locking
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this is the dedicated howto page for the extraction-layer concept first minted in kv-operations.json; this page's whole subject is CAS-based concurrency control, confirmed by re-reading rather than assumed ('CAS is an acronym for _Compare And Swap_, and is known as a form of optimistic locking.')

concepts.label: Pessimistic Locking (get-and-lock / unlock operations)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a structurally distinct mechanism from CAS: an explicit, time-bounded exclusive lock on a document rather than an opportunistic version check performed only at mutation time

concepts.label: Document
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - already promoted (concepts/data/document.json); this is the object that CAS values and locks apply to

relations.subject: sdk:pessimistic-locking
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted concurrency-control predicate for a subject taking an exclusive lock on an object before operating on it
relations.evidence: Documents can be locked using the _get-and-lock_ operation and unlocked either explicitly using the _unlock_ operation or implicitly by mutating the document with a valid CAS.

relations.subject: sdk:pessimistic-locking
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate whose object is frequently a literal rather than a concept
relations.evidence: Setting a lock greater than 30 seconds will cause Couchbase Server to set the lock duration at the Server's _default_ value, which is 15 seconds.

relations.subject: sdk:pessimistic-locking
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted comparative predicate for two strategies with opposite strengths/weaknesses; CAS is stated as the recommended default, pessimistic locking as the explicit alternative for stronger exclusivity guarantees
relations.evidence: While CAS is the recommended way to perform locking and concurrency control, Couchbase also offers explicit _locking_.

notable_absence.finding: The page's own retry loop for CasMismatchException is entirely manual application code (a `for` loop catching the exception and retrying up to `maxRetries` times), and never engages the SDK's own retry-classification mechanism (sdk:retry-strategy / RetryReason, documented in error-handling.md) - CAS mismatches are apparently not among the exceptions the SDK retries transparently on the application's behalf, but this page never states that connection either way, so it is left unasserted.
